instructions: Cut the cod into 2-inch chunks, pat them dry and sprinkle them with 1/2 tsp of the salt. Put them in the fridge.

Peel the potatoes and cut them into 3/4-inch cubes. Peel the carrots and slice them into thin rounds. Cut the onion into chunks, the celery into 1-inch pieces and the zucchini into chunks. Chop the tomato and thinly slice the 2 garlic cloves.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until it starts to soften.
Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds. Add the potatoes, carrots and zucchini and cook for 3 minutes, stirring.
Add 4 cups of hot water, the celery, the tomato, the remaining 1 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper. Turn the heat to high and bring it to a boil.
Turn the heat to medium and simmer for 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender when you poke them.
Lay the cod on top of the vegetables, cover and simmer gently for 8 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes when you press it.
Off the heat, squeeze in the juice of 1 lemon and stir gently so the fish doesn't break up too much. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Cut the other lemon into wedges. Serve in bowls with the lemon wedges.
method_notes: Vicki's Greek Recipes (4.3 from 3 votes, so under the 20 needed) is the lead: soften onion, add garlic, potatoes, carrots and zucchini, cover with water, then lay the fish on top and finish with lemon juice. Dimitra's Dishes cooks the fish first and strains the broth, which takes much longer; it also uses canned tomato. This version uses cod fillets instead of whole fish so it's done in under an hour, scales the lead down from 6 servings, and uses water rather than fish stock.
